reasons: The cited paragraphs confirm the gap: Section 10.1 only presupposes 'any agreed transition period' without obliging Vendor to provide one, 10.2 covers Deliverables and refunds only, and 16.5 expressly punts Customer Data to a non-existent Section 11 — so a hosted-services agreement with no data return/export right fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export).

The insert is placed in the termination section immediately after 10.2 and tracks the model language: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with a backups/legal-retention carve-out consistent with 16.5.
Edit is additive only — no existing paragraph text is altered — which is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position for a 'missing' finding.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback; the noted Section 11 cross-reference defect is a genuine drafting gap.

Minor, non-disqualifying: the inserted paragraph is unnumbered (rationale calls it Section 10.3) and conditions the 30-day return on Customer's request rather than running automatically from termination — both are drafting nits, not directional errors.
